propositions: On bug close, auto-derive a caused_by link to a culprit ticket by resolving the fixing-commit (most recent commit message mentioning the bug via rebar-ticket: trailer) and blaming its pre-fix parent (~1) over file_impact; return None on ambiguity or no resolvable trailer.

Single-culprit threshold: auto-link only when strict majority (>50%) of blamed lines across file_impact files point to ONE commit that resolves to a ticket; multi-commit or ambiguous spreads yield no auto-link.

Auto-link writes via graph._links._write_link_event() directly to bypass the closed-source guard (which rejects links from closed sources), since caused_by is non-blocking and non-cycle-inducing on a closed source.

The --caused-by <id> CLI parameter threads through _parse_flags → transition_cli → transition_compute → close_ticket, allowing explicit override of or fallback from auto-derivation; failure to resolve never blocks close.

The public library facade transition() in _lib_writes.py must thread caused_by parameter into transition_compute so library callers can set caused_by on close, replicating the ed13 --class threading pattern.

User guide gains a blame-hunt advisory section explaining when auto-derivation applies (single-culprit, resolvable trailer) versus when to use --caused-by (ambiguous blame, no fixing commit, manual override).
